string.text: DirectX 11, DirectX 12 or Vulkan: the same picture and effects. Frame generation needs DirectX 12. Takes effect after a game restart.
The GPU or its driver does not support DirectX 12 the way the game needs it, so only DirectX 11 is available.
Screen resolution. With AMD FSR or NVIDIA DLSS the game renders at a lower resolution and upscales to this one.
Frame rate cap. Spares the GPU when more frames are not needed.

Syncs frames to the monitor's refresh rate. On: no tearing, at the cost of a little input lag; a frame rate below the refresh rate is not cut down further. Adaptive: synced while the frame rate keeps up with the monitor, tearing instead of stutter when it falls below.

Overall graphics quality: draw and shadow distances, grass, reflections and effects. Anti-aliasing is a setting of its own. Higher is heavier on the GPU. On DirectX 12 the two highest presets shade flat and dark areas at a reduced rate.
Frees video and system memory after leaving a level. May make the next load slightly longer.
Smooths jagged edges. FXAA is the lightest and softest, SMAA is sharper, TAA is the smoothest: it builds the picture from several frames and is slightly softer in motion.
AMD FSR or NVIDIA DLSS does the anti-aliasing now. Turn them off to choose it here.

AMD FSR renders at a lower resolution and reconstructs the screen resolution: more FPS for a little sharpness. Native AA keeps the resolution and only anti-aliases. Works on any GPU. Replaces NVIDIA DLSS.
NVIDIA DLSS does what AMD FSR does, with the neural network of GeForce RTX cards. DLAA keeps the resolution and only anti-aliases. Replaces AMD FSR.
The GPU draws extra frames between the real ones: smoother motion, slightly more input lag. Works best from 60 FPS up. DirectX 12 and Vulkan only; the list holds what the GPU supports.

The GPU draws extra frames between the real ones: smoother motion, slightly more input lag. Works best from 60 FPS up. DirectX 12 only; the list holds what the GPU supports. On a GeForce RTX 40 or newer, NVIDIA DLSS needs Windows' hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling (Settings - System - Display - Graphics) turned on and a reboot.
Frame generation needs DirectX 12 or Vulkan: choose one under Renderer and restart the game.
The GPU or its driver does not support frame generation.
Sharpening after AMD FSR or NVIDIA DLSS: 0 adds none.
Sharpening for AMD FSR and NVIDIA DLSS: it works only while one of them is on.

DirectX 12: GTAO shading and water ripples are computed alongside the shadows and the G-buffer. Same image, a shorter frame where the graphics card gains from it; Auto turns it on only there (not on NVIDIA cards, where it measured slower).
The graphics card or driver has no separate compute queue.
DirectX 12: level textures load through Microsoft DirectStorage, so levels load faster. The picture is the same. Applies from the next load.
DirectStorage needs DirectX 12: choose it under Renderer and restart the game.
DirectStorage could not start on this system (its files are missing or Windows refused it): textures load the usual way.

Water and rain puddles reflect the world traced by the GPU's ray tracing cores: also what is off screen or hidden, out to the far shore. From Medium quality, wet and glossy surfaces reflect what surrounds them instead of the sky.

Sun shadows of buildings, terrain and other static objects are traced: exact at any distance, with soft edges. Trees, grass, characters and moving objects keep their shadow maps, so their shadows still sway in the wind.
Ambient occlusion from ray tracing instead of the screen-space one: contact shading also from what the screen does not show.

Resolution and reach of the ray traced effects. Low: hard shadows, half-resolution occlusion, shorter reflections, no reflections on glossy surfaces. High: full resolution and the farthest reflections.
Ray tracing needs DirectX 12 or Vulkan: choose one of them under Renderer and restart the game.
Ray tracing needs DirectX 12 or Vulkan and a GPU with hardware ray tracing.
The GPU or its driver has no hardware ray tracing (DXR 1.1, Vulkan ray queries): GeForce RTX, Radeon RX 6000 and newer, Intel Arc.
Quality of the ray traced effects: it matters only while one of them is on.
Image gamma: makes the midtones lighter or darker.
Image contrast: the difference between light and dark areas.
Image brightness: the whole picture lighter or darker.
Camera field of view, in degrees.
Field of view for hands and weapons: lower makes the weapon larger and closer, higher makes it smaller.
Grass height. Takes effect after the level reloads.
Brightness of the screen-space sun shafts. The two lowest presets have none.
Sharpens fine detail (LumaSharpen). 0 turns it off.
Strength of the glow around bright lights.
Colour fringing towards the frame edges, like a camera lens. None at the centre.
Blurs the distance: at the horizon, while reloading and when aiming without a scope.
Technicolor filter: a film palette over the whole picture.
Film grain over the picture, stronger in bright areas.
Share of red in the picture: 0.50 is neutral, higher adds red, lower takes it away.
Share of green in the picture: 0.50 is neutral, higher adds green, lower takes it away.
Share of blue in the picture: 0.50 is neutral, higher adds blue, lower takes it away.
Colour saturation: 0 leaves it as is, higher is richer, lower is paler.
